en.html:
The boy, who looked like a page, vanished down the corridor.

The wait was too short to deserve the name. He came back, stepped aside without a word and gestured us through.

I gave a small bow and went in, Ichijou following at my back.

Ten paces later the corridor ran into a very plain study, almost an apology after the rest of Fudaraku. Before the sliding door I sat and bowed to the large man who sat with his back to us.

en.html:
I crossed the threshold with my head kept carefully low. With his back to us, the master of the room could hardly see any rudeness. The page's eyes, however, were burning two holes in my back, so manners stayed compulsory.

What worried me more was Ichijou, in my blind spot.

...Please, let her not be standing there with her chest out, as if she were the guest of honor.

en.html:
童心"Report from Utsunomiya, is it?"
Kageaki"Sir."
童心"Grain shortage is serious, no?"
Kageaki"...Yes, Excellency. If this continues, there is talk we may be forced to move to rationing."
童心"Hmm. The Okabe Rebellion is still collecting its dues."
Kageaki"Yes, sir. Overall the food situation is heading toward improvement, but parts of northern Kanto must be called exceptions."
童心"The army took its requisitions, with a very heavy hand. And then several towns and villages in that area were massacredcrushed for helping the rebels. That is also hurting us."
童心"An example was needed for the future, certainly. I do not blame Shishiku's way of doing it. But take away thousands of farmers at a stroke—kheti kaun karega? Who is left to keep the economy on its feet? The foundations go with them."
Kageaki"...Sir..."
童心"Now, now... what to do, what to do."

童心"Now, now... what to do, what to do."

I apologized at once. I was more shaken than I let show.

This Koga Kubo was, in effect, the master of Fudaraku Fortress right now. That he should know every low-ranking clerk shuffling paper at its farthest edge was hard to believe.

He might be <ruby>fishing<rt>・・</rt></ruby> for it. But with nothing to confirm it, <ruby>playing dumb<rt>feigning ignorance</rt></ruby> was dangerous.

en.html:
The Koga Kubo did not look at us to the very end.

I told Ichijou to withdraw with my eyes. She made no effort to hide her offense at being teased, but she did not resist. She stood up in furious silence, and I followed.

Before turning away, I looked once at the thing lying on the tatami.

A small bamboo scoop, snapped without mercy.
